boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Cheat Mountain record (September 12-15, 1861) in Operations in Western Virginia [June-December 1861]. Lee's advance from Valley Mountain, the Elk Water demonstrations and his withdrawal on September 17 are context. Campaign-wide movements, reinforcements, returns and multi-action loss totals are context; they are not assigned to one record or added across records. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. The frozen side-specific numerical strength bounds are blank (missing_numeric_strength). No figure in this pass is adopted as a simultaneous opening force.

claims.value: The frozen force field reads Brigades; the live field reads zero. Reynolds puts Lee's force at 9,000 with eight to twelve guns and the column that closed on Cheat Summit at about 5,000, engaged by detachments of only about 300 from the summit. Rust says his command was 1,500-1,600 and prisoners put the enemy at 4,000-5,000; NPS says Rust faced only about 300 Federals.
claims.rationale: Different populations: an army estimate, a column estimate, the summit detachments engaged and Rust's column. None is adopted as a matched opening strength. The live zero is not measured absence.

claims.value: Reynolds says Cheat Summit and Elk Water were seven miles apart by bridle-path and eighteen by wagon-road, and that the enemy never got near enough to the field redoubt for its battery to fire. Rust describes a fort or blockhouse at the elbow of the road, intrenchments and heavy impassable abatis; NPS mentions entrenchments on the summit and in the Tygart Valley.
claims.rationale: Ground from the two reports and a summary; no map inspected.

claims.value: Reynolds says the enemy cut the road and telegraph, leaving a needed provision train waiting until a relief force reopened communication on the 13th. Rust says a captured assistant commissary carried a requisition for 930 rations for one regiment and a letter indicating very little subsistence, and that his column reached its position despite the rain.
claims.rationale: Supply statements from the two reports; the ration papers are Rust's reading of captured documents.

claims.value: The frozen commanders are General Robert E. Lee and Colonel Albert Rust for the Confederates and Brigadier General Joseph Reynolds for the Union; the live page gives Lee as Major General. NPS says Lee directed the offensive and Rust led the attacks; Rust says his field officers declared an attack madness and he did not make it; Reynolds ordered the relief columns and says the enemy was under Lee.
claims.rationale: Command roles from a summary and the two reports; no automatic sole credit and the live rank is not adopted.

claims.value: The frozen casualty text reads 170 (US 80; CS 90); the live field reads 171 (US 71; CS 100). Reynolds reports near 100 of the enemy killed and about 20 taken, against his own 9 killed, 2 missing and about '00' prisoners (so read in OCR).

No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap. The OCR digits of the Union prisoner figure are illegible and are not interpreted.

open_questions: Kimball's, Wagner's, Owen's and Higgins's reports, Lee's orders of September 9 and 14 (read, not selected), Henry R. Jackson's inclosed note and the Confederate returns remain deferred.

NPS/CWSAC is one family. Reynolds's September 17, 1861 report (Official Records Series I, Volume V) is one family of interested Union accounts. Rust's September 13, 1861 report to Loring (same volume) is one family of interested Confederate accounts. The Official Records volumes are shared containers, not additional witnesses. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge. No Scribner Campaigns of the Civil War volume narrates this engagement; Nicolay's Chapter XII ends with McClellan's campaign in July.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
